notes: Workspace units remaining was read live from subscription-info-limits-and-usage after the last call: 789384 of 800000 used, so 10616 left until the 8 October reset. That figure includes the parallel agent spending from the same pool. My own spend was 21903 of the 26000 budget, measured from the apiUsageCosts block returned with every call. Row cost was a flat 13 units; the difficulty field was never requested. Empty result sets still cost a 50 unit minimum.

Every volume, cpc and parentTopic in this file is a raw Ahrefs figure copied from a keywords-explorer-matching-terms response. Nothing is estimated or interpolated. No row has a null volume, so no row is excluded from the totals.
cpc is in USD cents as returned by Ahrefs. A null cpc means Ahrefs returned null, not zero.

Deduplicated against keyword-research.json, keyword-expansion-eu.json, keyword-expansion-asia.json and keyword-expansion-deep.json on country plus NFKC lowercased trimmed keyword. 59 rows were dropped as already present in those files and 0 as internal duplicates across my own seeds.

ro-ro is effectively barren for these clusters. "internet in strainatate", "internet în străinătate", "internet strainatate", "wifi aeroport" and "wifi lotnisko" style queries all returned zero rows. "străinătate" returns only jobs-abroad queries, "cartela sim" returns only hardware (routers, security cameras, smartwatches) and "internet mobil" returns only domestic Romanian operator plans. After the DROP rules only one Romanian keyword survives. Romania should be served from the shared English and destination pages, not from its own connectivity cluster pages.

The roaming cluster is the single biggest complementary find, but it is heavily polluted by domestic operator tariff queries which the brief tells me to drop. I dropped every row naming a national carrier (ee, o2, vodafone, three, giffgaff, sky, tesco, lebara, id mobile, voxi, smarty, bt, verizon, att, t mobile, us cellular, telekom, congstar, aldi talk, orange, sfr, free, bouygues, sosh, iliad, tim, wind, windtre, fastweb, postemobile, movistar, digi, lowi, yoigo, simyo, jazztel, masmovil, pepephone, euskaltel, finetwork, kpn, odido, ben, simpel, youfone, hollandsnieuwe, budget mobiel, plus, play, nju, plush). What remains is generic ("what is data roaming", "roaming aan of uit", "jak włączyć roaming") or destination-scoped ("roaming schweiz", "roaming w turcji", "roaming andorra"), both of which are legitimate Livdar targets.

Also dropped: bare competitor and rental brands (roamless, klook, japan wireless, sakura mobile, ninja wifi, ultralink, ecovox, novaltel, better roaming), device SKUs (inseego, gl.inet, mudi, asus, ryoko, tmohs1, jetpack, solax which is a solar inverter dongle not a travel device), home and appliance wifi (portable wifi box for home, portable wifi for gaming, condizionatore portatile wifi, cecotec aire acondicionado, scanner and imprimante portable wifi), laptop wifi troubleshooting (carte wifi pc portable, activar wifi en portatil, mi portatil no se conecta al wifi), streaming abroad (deutsches fernsehen im ausland, tv kijken in het buitenland, waipu tv, netflix abroad), banking abroad, study abroad admin, event and festival wifi hire, national roaming explainers (roaming krajowy), and starlink.

Judgement call worth auditing: the generic heads "portable wifi" (us, 20000), "mifi" (us, 7600), "mifi device" (us, 4300), "wifi portatile" (it, 6100) and "wifi portátil prepago" (es, 350) sit on a boundary. The brief lists pocket wifi, portable wifi and mifi as a seed cluster to KEEP, but in the US, Italian and Spanish markets a large share of that demand is domestic mobile broadband rather than travel. I kept the unbranded category heads and the explicitly travel-qualified long tail, and dropped every carrier-branded and device-model variant. If the audit disagrees, removing these five rows costs about 38350 volume.

Seed phrasing matters more than expected. The Ahrefs ro index requires diacritics and still returns nothing for the connectivity phrases; the pl index stores the diacritic forms ("internet za granicą" 800 vs "internet za granica" 350) so both were swept and both kept as distinct real keywords; the fr index stores apostrophes as spaces ("internet à l étranger").

Three rows in fr-fr are foreign language spillover that Ahrefs genuinely records in the France index: "roaming frankreich" (de), "roaming dati" (it) and "how to enable data roaming on iphone" (en). They are kept because the volume is real and the topic is in scope, but their language field is set to the market language, not the query language. The same applies to a handful of English and German roaming queries in the nl and it indexes.
Minimum volume filter was 20 throughout. Several seeds exhausted below the requested row limit, which is why some markets have fewer rows than the limit implies rather than being truncated.
en-us and en-gb share many keywords. They are separate rows because Ahrefs reports genuinely different volumes per country, and the dedupe key is country plus keyword.
